Expirations.description:
Net each strike over exactly these expirations (`YYYY-MM-DD`,
comma-separated) — one for a single-expiration heatmap (`2026-05-22`)
or several for a custom set (`2026-05-22,2026-06-19`). Supersedes
`maxExpirations`, and reaches any expiration the snapshot has, not just
the nearest ones. Requested dates the symbol does not have are ignored;
the `expirations` array in the response lists what was actually used.
If none of them match, the response is `404` with
`code: expiration_not_found` and the available dates in the message.
On `/v1/heatmap`, expirations that have already expired are not
available (they are trimmed from the live snapshot) — replay them with
`/v1/historical` instead.
Expirations.name: expirations

IncludeEmpty.description:
By default, an interior strike whose every returned cell is below 50 in
absolute value (listed but effectively untraded) is left out, judged on
the selected metric alone. So gamma and vanna for the same instant can
return different strike lists. The outermost strikes are never
removed. `true` keeps every strike in the window, so the list is the
snapshot's own contiguous ladder and is identical for gamma and vanna.
Not supported on the single-symbol stream (`symbol=`).
IncludeEmpty.name: includeEmpty

Layout.description:
`net` (default) returns one net value per strike. `matrix` also returns
`matrix`, the per-expiration grid those values are summed from.
Layout.name: layout

MaxExpirations.description:
How many of the nearest expirations to net into each strike's `value`:
an integer from 1 to 60, or `all`. Values above 60 return
`400 invalid_parameter`. Ignored when `expirations` is set.
MaxExpirations.name: maxExpirations

MaxStrikes.description:
Maximum number of strikes around spot to return: an integer from 1 to
1000, or `all` for every strike the snapshot lists (SPXW lists about
730). Values above 1000 return `400 invalid_parameter`; they are never
silently reduced. Values below 1 are treated as 1. The single-symbol
stream (`/v1/stream?symbol=`) accepts at most 400 and no `all`.
MaxStrikes.name: maxStrikes

Metric.description: Which Greek exposure to return per strike.
Metric.name: metric

Symbols.description:
One ticker, or a comma-separated list for a single cross-asset call
(e.g. `SPY` or `SPY,SPX,QQQ`). Each is returned as an element of
`data.symbols`. At most 10 distinct symbols (more → `400`
`invalid_parameter`). Unknown symbols in a list are omitted; if none
is available → `404` `symbol_not_found`.
Symbols.name: symbols

Forbidden.description:
Unknown, revoked or expired key (`forbidden`, from the gateway), or an
admin-suspended account (`account_suspended`).

GatewayTimeout.description:
The request did not finish in time (`gateway_timeout`). Refunded;
retry, or narrow the request.

NotFound.description:
Unknown symbol, no data available, or none of the requested
`expirations` exist for the symbol (`code: expiration_not_found`).

Unauthorized.description: Missing API key (`unauthorized`), sent by the gateway.

VolForbidden.description:
As `Forbidden`, or `not_entitled`: Tempest data is not enabled for this
account (it is in preview). Refunded.

VolUnavailable.description: Tempest data is loading (`warming_up`, with `Retry-After`) or not configured (`unavailable`). Refunded.

Attribution.description:
Whether and how this response's data may be published. See
`/legal/api#sharing`. An Agent or MCP client should never publish
data where `shareable` is false, regardless of `shareClass`.
`required`, `license`, `shareable` and `shareClass` are always sent
on `/v1/options/*` and absent from the short form.

shareClass.description: "raw" (e.g. option quotes, greeks) must never be auto-published.

complete.description: False for a session still in progress (today) or ended less than 30 minutes ago.

frames.description: 1-minute frames inside the session the values are computed from.

maxValue.description: Largest single cell in any frame.

minValue.description: Smallest single cell (strike x expiration) in any frame.

peakAbsMax.description: Maximum over frames of max(|smallest cell|, |largest cell|).

peakAbsMean.description: Mean over frames of max(|smallest cell|, |largest cell|).

value.description: Net exposure at this strike for the selected metric.

LevelsSummary.description:
Digest of the returned strikes for the selected `metric`. Covers only
the strikes between `lowStrike` and `highStrike` (set by `maxStrikes`,
`maxExpirations` and `expirations`), never the whole chain.

flip.description:
Where the running sum of `value`, from the lowest returned strike
upward, changes sign (linear interpolation between the bracketing
strikes; the crossing nearest spot when there are several). Null
when the running sum never changes sign within the window.

negativeWall.description: The strike with the most negative value, or null when none is negative.

netExposure.description: Sum of `value` over the returned strikes.

positiveWall.description: The strike with the largest positive value, or null when none is positive.

attribution.description:
How to credit this data. Most routes send the short form
`{text, url, terms}` ("Data: Skylit"). Routes whose data class the
licensing design (TERMS.md §5) tags explicitly — today,
`/v1/options/*` — send the full licensing shape instead. Can be
absent; do not infer sharing rules from the short form or from
its absence.

cached.description: True if served from the in-process cache.

delayMinutes.description: The delay applied when `delayed` is true.

delayed.description:
True when your plan's data is delayed and this latest-data request
was served as of `delayMinutes` ago (mode is then `historical`).
Absent on real-time plans.

resolution.description:
Time resolution of the data served: "1s" when every symbol came
from 1-second data, "1m" when any came from minute-resolution
history.

velocity.description: Average change per minute over 5 minutes.

gapCovered.description: True only if no symbol had a board published during the gap.

stateRestored.description: True when every symbol received a current snapshot.

lagged.description: True when newer boards replaced ones this client had not yet received (slow reader); this is the newest.

StreamSnapshot.description: /v1/stream v2 `snapshot` event payload — a SymbolHeatmap (without per-strike velocityPct) plus `lagged`.

nodeType.description: Skylit's node classification for this strike.

value.description: Net exposure for the selected `metric` at this strike (summed across the returned expirations).

velocityPct.description:
Live percent change of this strike's value over the velocity window.
Present on `/v1/heatmap` only; omitted on `/v1/historical`.

asOf.description: RFC3339 timestamp of the snapshot actually returned (nearest to the requested instant).

expirations.description: Expiration dates (YYYY-MM-DD) contributing to each strike's net value.

matrix.description:
Present only with `layout=matrix`. One row per entry in `strikes`,
one column per entry in `expirations`: `matrix[i][j]` is the
exposure at strike i for expiration j.

priceChange.description: The board's spot minus previous close (the board's spot, not `spot`, on `/v1/heatmap`).

spot.description:
On `/v1/heatmap`, the latest underlying price at the time of the
request, which can be newer than the board. On `/v1/historical`
and in stream frames, the spot the board was computed at. The
board's own spot is `previousClose + priceChange`.

strikes.description: Per-strike nodes, ordered by strike ascending.

symbol.description: Canonical ticker for the returned data.

frames.description: Snapshots in the window, oldest first.

axis.description: Id of the axis in `axes` these values are aligned to.

values.description: Net exposure per strike, aligned with the axis's `strikes`.

symbol.description: Canonical ticker for the returned data.

asOf.description: When Tempest computed the newest value in this response.

frozen.description: True while Tempest serves the previous close (outside regular hours).

marketState.description: US equity session at request time.

publishedAt.description: When Tempest last published to the API.

sessionDate.description: The trading session (ET) that asOf belongs to. The close state is stamped 15:59 ET and always belongs to its own session.

total.description: Rows matching the filters, before offset/limit.

VolSymbol.description:
One symbol. Besides these fields it carries the requested module(s)
as objects keyed `iv`, `term`, `cones`, `sigma`, `surface`, `tilt`,
`events` (null when Tempest has none for the symbol). Module field
names follow Tempest's own (snake_case). Quote-derived prices (fields
named `mid`, `*_mid`, `straddle*`, `forward`, `price`, and a contract's
`low`, `oi`, `vol`) are never present.

stale.description: In session, true when the reading is more than 20 minutes old.

bearerApiKey.description:
Skylit API key in the `Authorization` header
(`Authorization: Bearer <key>`). The bare key without `Bearer ` is
also accepted; `X-API-Key` is not.

info.description:
Skylit exposes its real-time options-Greeks (gamma / vanna) heatmaps as a
versioned public HTTP API, per strike, with the live velocity metric and
Skylit's node classification (King / Gatekeeper / etc.).

**Authentication.** Send your Skylit API key as a bearer token:

    Authorization: Bearer <key>

A request without an `Authorization` header gets `401`; an invalid,
revoked or expired key gets `403`.

The gateway also accepts the bare key in the same header
(`Authorization: <key>`); `Bearer` is the documented form. The key is not
read from `X-API-Key` or the query string: those requests get `401`.

**Credit metering.** Every chargeable request debits a fixed cost from
your credit balance:

| Endpoint        | Cost |
|-----------------|-----:|
| `/v1/heatmap`    | 1   |
| `/v1/gex/levels` | 1   |
| `/v1/historical` | 5   |
| `/v1/historical/range` | 25 |
| `/v1/stats/daily` | 5  |
| `/v1/stream`     | 1 per symbol to open + 1 per symbol per minute open |
| `/v1/account`, `/v1/symbols`, `/v1/openapi.json` | 0 |

`/v1/openapi.json` (this document) needs no key.

**Failed calls are free:** a request answered with any 4xx or 5xx status is
refunded, and its `X-Credits-Remaining` already reflects the refund.

New API accounts start with 5,000 credits; Pro, Protégé and Quant also get
25,000 included credits each month (`GET /v1/account` shows the balance).
Every chargeable response
carries `X-Credits-Remaining: <balance>`. Out of credits → `402`
`insufficient_credits`; an admin-suspended account → `403`
`account_suspended`. Top up via your account console.

**Rate limits.** Each key has a requests-per-minute limit set by the
account's plan (Pro, Protégé and Quant: 120 per key; invite: 60 per key),
counted across every Skylit API host. `GET /v1/account` returns it as
`limits.requestsPerMinute`; read it instead of hard-coding a number. Over
it the gateway answers `429` `rate_limited`. Responses carry
`X-RateLimit-Limit` (the key's limit), `X-RateLimit-Remaining` (requests
left in the current window) and `X-RateLimit-Reset` (Unix time, in
seconds, when the window resets). The gateway's `429` has no `Retry-After`: wait until
`X-RateLimit-Reset`. `429`s from the API itself (concurrency and stream
limits) carry `Retry-After`.

**Attribution.** Every response carries
`X-Skylit-Attribution: Data: Skylit (https://skylit.ai/?utm_source=api&utm_medium=attribution)`, JSON success
responses carry `meta.attribution`, and `/v1/stream`'s `connected` event
carries the same object. When you share or publish Skylit data, credit
"Data: Skylit" (https://www.skylit.ai/api-terms#attribution).

**Symbols.** Multi-symbol routes take at most 10 distinct symbols per
request; more is a `400` `invalid_parameter` (never silently truncated).
Unknown symbols in a list are omitted from `data.symbols`; if none of the
requested symbols is available the response is `404` `symbol_not_found`.

Live streams (`/v1/stream`) cost 1 credit per symbol to open plus 1 per
symbol per minute connected, and close after one hour.

**Resolution.** The heatmap is a 1-second time series. `/v1/heatmap` and
`/v1/historical` return the single snapshot at or before the requested
instant (`/v1/historical` to the second); `/v1/historical/range` returns
every snapshot in a window of up to 15 minutes. History goes back to
2023-03-28; `meta.resolution` reports the resolution actually served:
`"1s"`, or `"1m"` for the older history that is only stored once a minute.

**Board size.** By default `/v1/heatmap` returns 92 strikes around spot
and the nearest 5 expirations, and leaves out interior strikes whose cells
are all negligible. `maxStrikes=all&maxExpirations=all&includeEmpty=true`
returns the full board exactly as stored. Limits above a cap are a `400`,
never a silent reduction.

**Compression.** Send `Accept-Encoding: gzip` and JSON responses come back
gzip-compressed (typically 3-5x smaller). Streams are never compressed.

**Velocity is live-only.** The `velocityPct` field is present on
`/v1/heatmap` (live) and absent on `/v1/historical` (replay).

**Response shape.** Success → `{ "data": ..., "meta": { ... } }`; errors →
`{ "error": { "code": "...", "message": "..." } }`, including the ones
the gateway sends itself (`401`, `403`, `429`, `504`). Unknown paths are
`404` `not_found`. camelCase throughout.
`data.symbols` is always an array (one element per requested symbol), so a
single-symbol call and a multi-symbol "Trinity" call share one shape.
info.summary: Options-Greeks heatmaps as a public HTTP API.
info.title: Skylit Public API

get.description:
The calling key's account: status, balance (credits and US dollars at
$0.001 per credit), whether usage is unlimited, and the limits that
apply. Free.

streamSymbolsConcurrent.description: Symbols you may hold open at once across all streams (per server).

get.description:
The strikes Skylit classifies as nodes (king, gatekeeper, pika, barney,
significant) for up to 10 symbols, strongest first, with each level's
distance from spot. Same live source, filters and 5-second cache as
`/v1/heatmap`; 1 credit per request.

Each symbol also carries `summary`: total net exposure, the strongest
positive and negative strikes (the walls), and the flip level where
cumulative net exposure changes sign. It is computed from the strikes
this request returned, so widen `maxStrikes` for a wider view.

A call that cannot finish within 20 seconds answers `504`
`gateway_timeout` (refunded); retry, or request fewer symbols.

kingNode.description: The strongest king node, or null when none is classified.

get.summary: Key levels (classified nodes) for one or more symbols

get.description:
Current per-strike heatmap for one or more symbols at the latest
snapshot. Includes the live `velocityPct` per strike. Pass multiple
comma-separated symbols for a single cross-asset (Trinity) call, and
`expirations` to net each strike over specific expiration dates instead
of the nearest `maxExpirations`. A call that cannot finish within 20
seconds answers `504` `gateway_timeout` (refunded); retry, or request
fewer symbols.
get.summary: Live per-strike heatmap (one or more symbols)

get.description:
The latest snapshot at or before `at` for one or more symbols — same
shape as `/v1/heatmap` minus `velocityPct` (velocity is live-only),
including `layout=matrix` for the per-expiration grid. Precision is
1 second where 1-second history exists for that day and 1 minute
otherwise; `meta.resolution` says which. `at` may go back to
2023-03-28, where heatmap history begins (coverage per symbol varies;
`/v1/symbols` lists each symbol's first date). If no snapshot exists
at/near that instant the response is `404` with `code: no_data`.
A read that cannot finish within 20 seconds answers `504`
`gateway_timeout` (refunded); retry, or request fewer symbols.

parameters.description: RFC3339 instant to replay (e.g. `2026-03-05T10:01:00Z`). Not before 2023-03-28.
parameters.name: at

error.message: None of the requested expirations are available for SPY. Available: 2026-03-05, 2026-03-06, 2026-03-07.
No snapshot available for SPY at 2025-01-01T10:01:00Z.

404.description:
No snapshot at/near the requested instant, none of the requested
symbols is available, or none of the requested `expirations` exist
in that snapshot.

get.summary: Replay — per-strike heatmap at a past instant (one or more symbols)

get.description:
Every snapshot between `from` and `to` (inclusive) for up to 5
symbols, at the stored resolution — one per second where 1-second
history exists (`meta.resolution: "1s"`), otherwise one per minute.
Each frame's `values[i]` is the net exposure at
`axes[frame.axis].strikes[i]`, summed over that axis's expirations —
the same number `/v1/historical` reports as `strikes[i].value` for
that instant. Axes are listed once and referenced by id; a new axis
appears only when the visible strikes or expirations change (the
strike window follows spot). Plain JSON numbers; responses are
gzip-compressed when the request sends `Accept-Encoding: gzip`.

**Cost:** 25 credits per call.

parameters.description: RFC3339 start of the window (inclusive). Up to 365 days back.
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: RFC3339 end of the window (inclusive). At most 15 minutes after `from`, not in the future.
parameters.name: to

200.description: Every snapshot in the window, per symbol.

get.summary: Replay — every snapshot in a window (up to 15 minutes, 5 symbols)

get.description: No key required. Free.

200.description: OpenAPI 3.1 document for the Skylit Public API.

get.description:
Per symbol and US trading session (ET): board spot open/high/low/close,
the smallest and largest single cell of the session, and the mean and
maximum over the session's frames of `max(|smallest cell|, |largest cell|)`
(a measure of how concentrated the exposure is, useful for ranking a
universe). Computed from 1-minute history, so every frame is one minute
apart (`frames` counts them). Weight `peakAbsMean` by `frames` to
average across days.

**Sessions.** `date` is the ET session date. By default a row covers
the regular session, 09:30-16:00 ET (frames stamped 09:30 up to
15:59); `extended=true` covers 04:00-20:00 ET instead, including
pre- and post-market. Weekends and NYSE market holidays have no
session and no row, including for indices whose heatmap updates
around the clock (SPX, SPXW, NDX, VIX). On early-close days the
session simply has fewer frames. `firstAt`/`lastAt` are UTC
timestamps. Today's row has `complete: false` until 30 minutes after
the session ends, and changes as the session goes on.

Up to 50 symbols, 31 calendar days and 400 symbol-sessions (symbols x
trading days) per call. Sessions with no data are omitted; a symbol
with none is omitted. Served from the historical file store; finished
sessions are cached, so repeat and overlapping calls are fast.
**Cost:** 5 credits per call.

parameters.description: Comma-separated tickers (up to 50).
parameters.name: symbols

parameters.description: First session date (`YYYY-MM-DD`, ET), not before 2023-03-28.
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: Last session date (`YYYY-MM-DD`, ET), inclusive. Default today (ET); at most 31 calendar days after `from`.
parameters.name: to

parameters.description: Cover the extended session (04:00-20:00 ET) instead of the regular session (09:30-16:00 ET).
parameters.name: extended

get.summary: Daily statistics per symbol (ranking and spot range)

get.description:
A **Server-Sent Events** (`text/event-stream`) feed of live per-strike
heatmaps. Two wire formats:

- **v2** (default with `symbols=`, or `format=v2`): up to 10 symbols on
  one connection, camelCase events matching `SymbolHeatmap`, resumable
  with `Last-Event-ID`.
- **v1** (default with `symbol=`): the original single-symbol format,
  unchanged.

### v2 events

Every event names its `symbol` (except connection-level events).

| Event | `id:` | Payload |
|---|---|---|
| `connected` | — | `{format:"v2", symbols, metric, creditsRemaining, creditsPerMinute, maxDurationSeconds}` |
| `resumed` | yes | Only when `Last-Event-ID` was sent. See *Resume*. |
| `snapshot` | yes | `StreamSnapshot` (= `SymbolHeatmap` + `lagged`). Once per symbol on connect, then on every board change. |
| `velocity` | yes | `StreamVelocity`: per-node velocity for the stream's `metric`, when it changes (checked every ~3s). |
| `symbol_unavailable` | — | `{symbol, reason: "no_live_board" \| "expiration_not_found", message}`; a `snapshot` follows once a board exists. |
| `credits` | — | `{remaining, charged}` after each per-minute debit. |
| `closed` | — | `{reason: "insufficient_credits" \| "account_suspended" \| "key_revoked" \| "monthly_cap_reached" \| "credit_check_failed"}`; stream ends. `key_revoked`: an API key on the account was revoked after this stream opened (streams opened on another still-valid key close too; reconnect to continue). `monthly_cap_reached`: the account's monthly spend cap was reached. |
| `reconnect` | yes | `{reason: "max_duration" \| "server_shutdown"}`; stream ends, reconnect with `Last-Event-ID`. |
| `: ping` | — | SSE comment every 15s so idle proxies (CloudFront: 60s) keep the connection. |

Snapshots differ from `/v1/heatmap` in two ways: `spot` is the board's
own spot, and strikes carry no `velocityPct` (use the `velocity`
event). Within a symbol, `asOf` never goes backwards; a board already
sent is never re-sent.

**Event ids (resume cursor).** The `id:` is the connection's position
in **every** symbol, not just the event's: a comma-separated list of
`SYMBOL:asOfUnixMs`, e.g. `SPY:1790000000123,QQQ:1790000000456`.
`asOfUnixMs` is the board's publish timestamp, identical on every
server, so a cursor resumes on any pod. Per symbol it never decreases
and strictly increases with each `snapshot` for that symbol.

**Resume.** Reconnect with header `Last-Event-ID: <last id>` (browsers'
`EventSource` does this automatically) or `?lastEventId=`. The server
keeps no event history: boards are full state, so it sends the
`resumed` event and then a fresh `snapshot` for every symbol that has a
live board, whether or not it changed. Per symbol `status` is:
`unchanged` (no board was published during the gap — nothing missed),
`advanced` (at least one board was published; intermediate boards are
**not** replayed, only the latest), `unknown` (symbol not in the
cursor), or `unavailable` (no live board right now). `gapCovered` is
true only if every symbol is `unchanged`; `stateRestored` is true when
every symbol received a current snapshot. Velocity is not replayed; the
latest reading is re-sent when this server has one.

**Backpressure.** A client that reads slower than boards are published
is never queued behind: each symbol holds at most one pending board, a
newer board replaces it, and the board that is finally sent carries
`lagged: true`. A client that stops reading for 30s is disconnected.

**Pricing (v2).** `N` = number of symbols. `N` credits on connect
(charged before the SSE upgrade, so an under-funded client gets a clean
`402`), then `N` credits per minute open — 1 credit ($0.001) per symbol
per minute, i.e. $0.06 per symbol-hour, plus $0.001 per symbol to open.
Minutes are charged in advance and a partial minute is not refunded.

**Limits.** At most 10 symbols per connection (more → `400`). At most
25 symbols per customer per server across all open streams (a v1
stream counts as 1); over it → `429` `stream_limit_reached` with
`Retry-After: 2` (a just-closed stream frees its symbols within about
a second). v1 also keeps its 5-streams cap. Each server streams a
bounded number of **distinct** symbols across all customers (default
20); a v2 stream that would add a new symbol beyond that gets `503`
`stream_capacity` with `Retry-After: 5` — retry (you may land on
another server). Symbols already being streamed are always admitted.
Streams end after 1 hour with `reconnect`.

### v1 events (single symbol, unchanged)

`connected` `{symbol, creditsRemaining}`, `initial_data`,
`snapshot_update`, `velocity_update` (internal PascalCase board shape),
`credits`, `closed`, `reconnect`, and a `: keepalive` comment every
30s. 1 credit to open + 1 per minute. v1 rejects `expirations`.

> OpenAPI cannot fully model an event stream. See
> https://www.skylit.ai/docs/api-reference/rate-limits-and-retries (Streams).

get.summary: Live SSE stream (up to 10 symbols per connection)

get.description:
Every symbol the API serves: whether it is an index, previous tickers
after a rename (still accepted as input), the metrics available, and
the UTC dates its history covers (`null` when coverage could not be
read). History dates are refreshed every few hours. Free.

Tempest Cones: the move the options market prices for each horizon
(`close`, `1d`, `week`, `opex`, `30d`), as 1-sigma percent and price bands
around spot (from implied variance), plus the level set drawn on the
chart. A horizon that does not exist at that moment (the `close`
horizon after hours) is null.
**Two different questions.** `horizons[]` is priced from the current
spot: how much further options price the move from *now* to each
settle. It moves with price, so it is not a budget to measure a move
against. `levels[]` is priced at a past close and does not move
intraday: read how far a move has gone against `hi1` / `lo1` (1-sigma)
and `hi2` / `lo2` (2-sigma).

**Levels** (`levels[]`): `day` (the prior close, to today's close),
`week` (last week's final close, to this week's last close) and `month`
(the last monthly options expiration's close, to the next monthly
expiration's close). Each has `name`, `label`, `anchor`, `priced_at`,
`until`, `em1_pct` and `hi1`/`lo1`/`hi2`/`lo2`. A level is absent when
its anchor close has no reading.

**Per horizon** (`horizons[]`): `name`, `minutes` to the settle,
`em1_pct` (1-sigma, % of spot), `em1` / `em2` (1- and 2-sigma in price),
`realized_em_pct` (20-day realized vol over the same span). Optional,
null when not available, and absent on older readings:
- `up1_pct`, `dn1_pct`, `up2_pct`, `dn2_pct`: the move to each side in %
  of spot as the options' skew prices it (put skew makes the downside
  wider). Null: read `em1_pct` both ways.
- `tail_src`: how the 2-sigma sides were read: `quantile` (from the
  fitted smile, within the quoted strikes) or `wing` (twice the 1-sigma
  side, which understates a steep tail).
- `skew_expiry`: the expiration whose smile set that shape.
- `events[]`: scheduled events inside the horizon (after `asOf`, at or
  before the settle), each `{kind, label, at, timing, jump_pct,
  var_share}`: `kind` is `earnings`, `fomc`, `cpi` or `nfp`; `at` is the
  ISO-8601 instant it is modelled at; earnings add `timing` (`bmo` /
  `amc`), `jump_pct` (the report's own implied move, %) and `var_share`
  (the share of the horizon's priced variance that is the report, 0-1).
- `event_adjusted`: true when this horizon's move includes an earnings
  report.
Response: `data.symbols[]` has `symbol`, `asOf`, `sessionDate`, `stale` and `cones`.
Symbols Tempest does not cover are listed in `data.missing`. **Cost:** 1 credit per call (up to 10 symbols).

daily SVX30/SVX1D (plain and adjusted), close and risk reversal, the
point-in-time usual-range band (`p20`/`p50`/`p80`, each day's band
from the 252 sessions before it), earnings-eve sessions, realized vs
implied (`ivrv`: 20-day realized vol, VRP series, current VRP and

Tempest Catalyst: the next earnings date and timing, the move priced into it
(`implied_move_pct`, from the implied-variance term structure across the event;
null when only a straddle estimate exists, `estimate: true`), the median and mean past earnings moves and how the
implied move compares, the report-by-report record, and the volatility risk
premium (`vrp`: expected VRP and its percentile, 20-day realized vol,
trailing overpaid share). `events` is null for symbols without a scheduled event.

get.description:
One row per stored session, at that session's close (15:59 ET): OHLC,
SVX per tenor and weekend-adjusted, ATM vol, term slope,
30-day risk reversal / butterfly / ATM vol / skew slope, tilt, chain
depth (`n_used`), `calc_v`. Columnar: `dates[]` plus one array per
field in `columns`. Every value was knowable at that session's close;
features from session D predict D+1 onward. History starts where
Tempest's backfill does (up to about two years); `/v1/vol/symbols`
shows each symbol's last stored session.

**Cost:** per symbol-day: 1 credit per 10 symbol-weekdays in the
requested window, rounded up, minimum 1 (1 symbol x the default month
is 3; 10 symbols x one year is 261). Computed from the request, so
known before the call; holidays are not discounted.

get.description:
SVX, Tempest's constant-maturity implied volatility per symbol (a VIX-style
variance-strip reading on the symbol's own option chain), in annualised vol
points: `svx1d`, `svx9`, `svx30`, `svx3m`, `svx6m`, each also weekend-adjusted
(`*_adj`, the weekly calendar pattern removed). Plus IV rank and percentile
(`iv_rank`, `iv_pct`, over the trailing year, on the adjusted reading),
1y/3y/5y percentiles per tenor (`pct_by`), the one-year range, the ratio to the
VIX (`ratio_vix`, `ratio_z`), term slope and curve state, and historical
mean-reversion odds (`reversion`). `quality` / `thin` flag shallow chains.
Response: `data.symbols[]` has `symbol`, `asOf`, `sessionDate`, `stale` and `iv`.
Symbols Tempest does not cover are listed in `data.missing`. **Cost:** 1 credit per call (up to 10 symbols).

get.description:
The market-wide volatility read: VIX1D, VIX9D, VIX, VIX3M, VIX6M, VVIX
and SKEW (computed by Tempest from SPX and VIX option chains), their
ratios and one-year percentiles, the VIX-forward curve state and roll
(`vx_curve_state`, `vx_roll_pct`, `vx_m1_vs_vix_pct`; the curve's price
points are not served), regime and crowded-calm flags,
Mag-7 vs QQQ dispersion, a Fear & Greed score with its components, and
120 sessions of history for the main series. **Cost:** 1 credit.

Tempest Radar: one row per covered symbol with its headline readings
(SVX term and percentiles, IV rank, ratio to VIX, term slope, skew,
tilt, expected move, running sigma and odds, next event and VRP,
options volume, sector, `quality`). Thin chains are not ranked.
Filter with `min_<field>` / `max_<field>` on any sortable field, and
`curve`, `sector`, `quality` (exact match). Unknown parameters are a
`400`. Rows missing the sort field sort last. **Cost:** 5 credits per
call (up to 500 rows).

parameters.description:
Field to sort by (default `svx30`): svx30, svx1d, svx30_pct_1y,
svx1d_pct_1y, svx9_pct_1y, svx3m_pct_1y, iv_rank, iv_pct, ratio_vix,
term_slope, rr25_30, skew_pct_1y, tilt_21, tilt_z, tilt_pct_1y,
em_1d_pct, running_sigma, sigma_odds_pct, expected_vrp,
event_move_pct, days_to_event, opt_vol, spot, spot_vol_corr,
cheap_from_low_pct, day_pace, day_reprice.
`day_pace` is today's move against the priced one-day move for the
time elapsed, in sigma; `day_reprice` is the one-day range options
price now over what they priced at the prior close for the rest of
the day (above 1: implied vol bid). Both are null outside regular
hours.

get.description:
When Tempest last computed (`asOf`), the session it belongs to
(`sessionDate`), whether it is serving the frozen close state
(`frozen`: outside regular hours nothing is recomputed, because
after-hours option quotes are too wide to read), the market state now,
how many symbols are published and coverage counts. Free.
get.summary: Tempest freshness, coverage and market state (free)

get.description:
Pushes a symbol's full module state each time Tempest recomputes it:
about every minute for the most active names and every ~10 minutes for
the rest during regular hours; nothing outside them (the close state
stays frozen). Events: `connected`, `vol` (id = asOf in epoch ms; data
is a `data.symbols[]` element of `/v1/vol/snapshot`), `market` (with
`market=true`), `credits`, `closed`, `reconnect` (after an hour).
Resume with `Last-Event-ID` (or `lastEventId`): the initial burst skips
symbols whose asOf is older than it; a frame at exactly that id may
repeat. Up to 10 symbols per stream and 5 streams per account. Each
server also holds a bounded number of open streams across all
customers; at capacity → `503` `stream_capacity` with `Retry-After: 5`
(retry; you may land on another server). Access is re-checked every
minute: a stream closes with `closed` `{"reason":"access_withdrawn"}`
once the account is no longer enabled.
**Cost:** 1 credit to connect and 1 per minute open.

tags.description:
Tempest, Skylit's volatility suite: implied vol per symbol (SVX), term
structure, expected-move cones, sigma move tracking, surface and skew,
call/put premium tilt, event vol and VRP, the S&P volatility complex, a
universe screener and daily history. Precomputed by Tempest; every
response states when (`asOf`) and for which session (`sessionDate`).
In preview: `403 not_entitled` until enabled for your account.

These endpoints serve derived analytics only: implied vols, skews,
ratios, z-scores, ranks and percent moves. Option prices and price
levels read from option quotes (contract mids, straddle prices or moves,
forwards, the VIX-forward curve) are not part of any /v1/vol response.
